title: A Choir for the Room
premise: Coral Reyes takes a teaching post at Marrowfen School, where a class vanished decades ago and the town's polite silence is treated as a curriculum. When frost excavations uncover a door sealed from the inside beneath the east wing, the missing class begins returning—singing in the corridors at night—and Coral, the school's only committed skeptic, must lead the remaining staff and students through a single night of siege. The truth she refuses to accept is that the school itself was built as an invitation, and her own arrival was foretold in the founding ledgers. At dawn, Coral chooses to walk through the door as the choir's new voice, sealing it from the inside herself and buying the town one more generation of borrowed time.
about_author: Beatrix Underhill is a former rural schoolteacher who spent eleven years in northern boarding schools before turning to horror full-time. She writes in the margins of her students' old exercise books, which she refuses to explain.

chapters.title: First Bell
chapters.summary: Coral Reyes arrives at Marrowfen School in late autumn, taking over a classroom no one will explain is vacant. POV: Coral. She notes the frost patterns on the windows that no one scrapes away. Emotional beat: wary optimism curdling into unease as the staff greet her with rehearsed warmth and one too many apologies.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Coral's class roster lists thirty-one students; thirty attend. The missing desk belongs to a boy named Ellery Voss, and no record of him exists anywhere. POV: Coral. The caretaker, Mr. Halloway, tells her to stop counting. Emotional beat: the first crack in her rationalism—she counted twice.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: During morning roll call, a voice answers 'here' for Ellery from the empty desk. Coral investigates the school archives and finds the 1974 register with the same name crossed out in red. POV: Coral, with a brief interlude from Halloway's journal. Emotional beat: dread dressed up as administrative curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Town Agreed To
chapters.summary: Coral visits the village pub and meets Ida Marsh, whose sister was in the vanished class of '74. Ida warns her that the school sits on 'borrowed ground' and that the town pays rent in silence. POV: Coral, then Ida. Emotional beat: the skeptic meets the first true believer and hates how calm Ida is.

chapters.title: Excavation
chapters.summary: A frost-damage repair crew opens the east wing's foundations and strikes something that isn't foundation: a stone door, its iron ring fused, sealed from the inside. The foreman's dog refuses to approach. POV: rotating—foreman Bram, Coral, a student named Priya. Emotional beat: collective thrill that curdles when the door is warm to the touch.

chapters.title: The Singing Starts
chapters.summary: That night, Coral hears children's voices harmonizing in the corridors. She follows the sound to the east wing and finds thirty-one sets of small footprints in the frost, all leading to the door, none returning. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: her disbelief begins costing her sleep, then her certainty.

chapters.title: Priya's Essay
chapters.summary: A student, Priya Nandakumar, submits an essay describing a dream of a classroom under the school where the desks face the wrong way. Her handwriting matches the 1974 register's. POV: Priya, then Coral. Emotional beat: Coral realizes the past isn't haunting the school—it's recruiting.

chapters.title: The Founding Ledgers
chapters.summary: Coral breaks into the headmaster's office and finds ledgers from 1891: the school's founders didn't build on the ground, they built the door a congregation. Each generation's register lists one 'invited' name. The 2024 page already reads: C. REYES. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the skeptic's worst fear—that she was always expected.

chapters.title: Halloway's Vigil
chapters.summary: Coral confronts the caretaker, who admits his family has kept the door watched for ninety years. The rent in silence was real: as long as no one acknowledged the choir, it stayed below. The excavation broke the agreement. POV: Halloway. Emotional beat: guilt and resignation; he's been waiting decades to hand off the watch.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Loss
chapters.summary: The foreman, Bram, is found at the sealed door, frostbitten from the inside out, smiling, humming a tune Coral now recognizes as the school song in a minor key. The door's seal has begun to breathe. POV: Coral and Priya. Emotional beat: the threat becomes physical; the town's denial becomes complicity.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Coral convinces the headmaster to keep the students overnight as a storm seals the roads. She organizes the east wing's evacuation, but eleven students are missing from the count—and their desks are warm. POV: Coral, with staff meeting interludes. Emotional beat: leadership under siege; her skepticism converts to strategy.

chapters.title: The Class of '74
chapters.summary: Ida Marsh arrives through the storm with her sister's diary. The vanished class didn't disappear; they were 'promoted'—chosen to sing the door's maintenance hymn so it stays shut. One voice retires each generation. Ellery was this generation's. POV: Ida, diary excerpts. Emotional beat: grief reframed as duty; the missing aren't victims, they're garrison.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: The remaining students begin sleep-singing in unison, and Coral realizes the choir below is teaching them the hymn through the frost on the windows. She tries earplugs, sedatives, separation—nothing holds. POV: Priya, who can now sight-read the hymn from the frost patterns. Emotional beat: horror of the body betraying the will; Coral's guilt sharpens.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: The ledgers' final page reveals the truth: in 1891 the founders didn't seal something out—they invited something in to keep something worse out, and the choir feeds it so it keeps its bargain. The door is a mouth, and the school is its keeper. POV: Coral and Halloway together. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—the horror is also the shield.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Inward
chapters.summary: At midnight the seal fails. The eleven missing students return, unaged, singing perfectly, and walk the living students toward the open door like an ushering line. Coral breaks the line with fire alarms and floodlights—the entity recoils from ordered noise, from bells. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the skeptic's tools become the town's salvation.

chapters.title: Bells
chapters.summary: Coral weaponizes the school: every bell, buzzer, and metronome rung in rounds to hold the entity at the threshold. Halloway is taken mid-vigil, smiling, joining the choir. The hymn below changes—it's now learning Coral's name. POV: rotating staff and students. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity; the cost is counted in colleagues.

chapters.title: The Bargain Re-Read
chapters.summary: Coral finds the founders' addendum: the door can be resealed from the inside only, by a voice the ledger names, sung willingly. The frost on every window now spells her name. Sunrise is the deadline; after dawn, the invitation becomes a claim. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the trap and the choice arriving as the same sentence.

chapters.title: Ida's Refusal
chapters.summary: Ida offers herself in Coral's place, claiming the ledger will accept any Marsh—the family that signed first. The frost rejects her; the invitation was specific. Coral understands the school hired her the way a trap is baited. POV: Ida, then Coral. Emotional beat: sacrifice refused; Coral stops being a bystander in her own story.

chapters.title: Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Coral spends the small hours teaching her students the counter-hymn—the bells' pattern set to words—to be sung after she's gone, so the seal holds a generation. Priya writes it into the register under Coral's name. POV: Coral and Priya. Emotional beat: a teacher's final class; grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: Through the Door
chapters.summary: At first light's edge, Coral walks the corridor of frost footprints, singing the invitation willingly, and the door takes her. The choir's hymn resolves; the eleven children return to their beds, unremembering; the door seals, warm, from the inside. POV: Coral, ending mid-verse. Emotional beat: terror and terrible peace braided together.

chapters.title: Roll Call
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Marrowfen reopens. The frost no longer forms patterns. Priya, now the register-keeper, calls roll and a new voice answers 'here' from Coral's old desk—present, patient, keeping the watch. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: mourning that is also gratitude; the cycle acknowledged, not broken.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Room
chapters.summary: Years on, Priya leads the school, and each winter the students sing the counter-hymn at the east wing wall. Beneath the floor, faint and contented, thirty-two voices answer in harmony—one of them teaching the newer ones the melody Coral taught it. POV: Priya, closing. Emotional beat: belonging redefined—Coral didn't vanish; she was enrolled.
